name: Edgar cut

lead: The Edgar cut is a haircut with straight, blunt bangs across the forehead and tapered sides. It changes the frame of the face: the fringe covers the forehead and hairline while the taper keeps the sides short.
It began in Latino communities in US border states and spread among Gen Z and Millennials in the 2010s and 2020s. On looksmax.org, members discuss it as a way to cover a receding hairline.

paras: Barbers cut a low or mid taper at the sides and leave the top long enough to comb forward into a straight fringe. It can be worn with straight, wavy or curly hair.
No health risk, but reception varies: some people link it to gang culture, and El Salvador banned it in public schools in 2025.

lead: The Edgar cut, also called the Edgar haircut, is a style with straight, blunt bangs across the forehead and short tapered sides, associated with Latino culture and worn with any hair texture, including wavy and curly hair. It has been compared to the bowl cut. [1]

For appearance, the cut works through framing: the fringe sits low across the forehead and hairline while the taper keeps the sides short and clean. In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a way to cover a receding hairline, with one thread describing a low taper, a grown-out top and a forward comb to meet the thinning front. [2]

The style is tied to the takuache subculture and to U.S. border states, and spread widely in the 2010s and 2020s, helped by TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. News coverage describes both enthusiasm among young wearers and stereotyping, and El Salvador banned it in public schools in 2025. [1][3] Its name's origin is unconfirmed. [1]
infobox: Latino communities in US border states; name's origin unconfirmed [1]

paras: The cut is usually described as straight bangs with tapered sides and works with any hair texture. [1] NBC News describes it as a bowl-like cut with a line-up and tapered sides, and notes variants such as the Fluffy Edgar. [3]
Barbers interviewed by NBC said some colleagues struggle with the cut or decline to do it; one Texas barber said he cut about seven a day and believed it is "here to stay". [3]

The name's origin is unconfirmed and is often linked, according to Wikipedia wrongly, to former Seattle Mariners player Edgar Martinez. [1] NBC News relays a popular story in which a barber, Anthony Reyes, was asked to shape a design of Martinez on a client's head and posted a viral video of a similar cut. [3]

The style is tied to takuaches, a Mexican-American subculture of truck enthusiasts (the trokiando scene, with cowboy hats, boots, pickups and Mexican music), and is sometimes called the takuache cut. It was first popular in Texas, New Mexico, Arizona and California. In the Rio Grande Valley it is slangily called 'the cuh'. Commentators have also noted a resemblance to hairstyles of Indigenous peoples such as the Jumano. [1][3]

Social media, especially TikTok, along with YouTube and Instagram, spread the look beyond the border states among Gen Z and younger Millennials, and memes featuring cartoon and film characters amplified it. [3] NBC News published its feature on 8 March 2023. [3]
A University of Texas at El Paso professor called it a 'really big marker of this generation', while a Corpus Christi barber said it is 'not a favorite amongst parents'. [1]

NBC News reports that viral videos and memes often mock wearers over their looks, clothing and speech, and quotes associate professor Alexandro Gradilla linking the style to Indigenous identity and to rasquachismo, an aesthetic sometimes dismissed as unrefined. [3] Some critics link the cut to gang culture; a San Antonio restaurant owner banned it, and a San Antonio bar owner's anti-Edgar stance prompted backlash and a mural on the haircut's Indigenous roots in 2024. [1]

El Salvador banned the cut in public schools in August 2025 under a directive from Education Minister Karla Trigueros. Wikipedia notes that in Turkiye a similar haircut has been linked to youth violence. [1]
On looksmax.org, a thread on the cut for balding men advises a low taper with the top grown out and combed forward, and cutting the front to blend with the remaining hair. [2]
Wikipedia lists the bowl cut and the Caesar cut as related haircuts. [1]

lore.intro: Members discuss the Edgar cut mainly as a hairline-concealing option. [2]

claims.claim: The Edgar cut hides a receding hairline
